value.summary: The s04 follow-ups split from plan 206 on the prime's instruction: record closed seats in lineage (F15), batch assign (F16), zoned dates (F13), the two-role window name (F17), the writer's index.lock marker and retry (F18), and the #122 same-second test (F003).

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Split from plan 206 (06 Nov). Sources: #122's review (F003), the wave B dogfood (F13, F15, F16), pm-001's holder assigns (F17), and the prime (F18). Under the prime's ruling, the F003 test is deleted in a one-line PR on its first CI failure; if that happens before this plan, AC for F003 restores a deterministic version.

sections.name: goals
value: The s04 follow-ups split from plan 206 on the prime's instruction: record closed seats in lineage (F15), batch assign (F16), zoned dates (F13), the two-role window name (F17), the writer's index.lock marker and retry (F18), and the #122 same-second test (F003).

sections.name: non_goals
value: Anything another roadmap step owns; see roadmap 001.

value.claim: F15, lineage import. `pij directory lineage add <role>[/<instance>] <seat> --from <time> --to <time> --why <text>` lets the prime record a closed seat's past holding (no live seat needed), validated against overlaps; refused for anyone but the prime.
value.receipt: assets/evidence/phase-1.md: lineage add: HTTP test, one commit, 9 launches

value.claim: F16, batch assign. `pij directory assign --batch <file>` (role, instance, seat lines) records many holders in one writer commit, all or nothing.
value.receipt: assets/evidence/phase-1.md: assign --batch: HTTP test, one commit for 3 holdings, 12 launches

value.claim: F003, the latent flake. The same-second HTTP test from #122 stops assuming a wall-clock second (inject the clock or drop the precondition) and keeps proving that rapid assign, release and reassign never collide.
F13, zones. Changelog and holder dates written by the writer carry an explicit zone (RFC 3339 with offset or Z), and the view prints the local time with its zone.
value.receipt: assets/evidence/phase-1.md: zoned dates written and rendered locally; unit test

value.claim: F18 (low, from the prime): a hand commit in the standing governance worktree can fail on index.lock while the daemon's writer is committing there (seen 06 Nov: the prime's commit raced the close writer's 655c0b6). While it holds the index, the writer leaves a short-lived marker naming itself (for example .git/pij-writer.owner with seat, pid and time, removed on exit); the community README tells humans to retry after a moment when they see it; and the writer's own commits retry briefly on a foreign index.lock (bounded), then refuse by name.
value.receipt: assets/evidence/phase-1.md: writer marker and bounded retry; writer test

value.claim: F17 (low): a seat holding two roles gets the last assign's window name. The window is named for the seat's primary holding (the earliest open one), or `<project>:<role1>+<role2>`; pick one, and say so in the docs.
value.receipt: assets/evidence/phase-1.md: first holding keeps the window; HTTP test and private run

value.claim: F24 (low, pm-001, 06 Nov): `just shared-build`'s owner file records `seat=<user>` because PIJ_ID is unset in harness seats, so a lock holder can't be told apart (seen: seat=jordanknight for warbler's run). The recipe takes the seat id from the pij registration of its caller (`pij whoami` or the daemon's view of the calling pid) when PIJ_ID is unset, and falls back to the user only outside a seat.
value.receipt: assets/evidence/phase-1.md: owner names the seat; shared-build test

value.claim: Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). Batch assign is one writer commit for many holders; lineage add is one commit; the writer's lock retry is bounded and only on a foreign lock. No timer or poll.
value.receipt: assets/evidence/phase-1.md: one commit per batch or lineage add; skipped rename launches nothing; no timer or poll

value.claim: Docs and states. No roadmap state change (follow-up work). docs/difficulties.md: F13, F15, F16, F17, F18 and #122 F003 marked resolved. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents new verbs and refusals; the skill's verb coverage tables carry them; `just ddocs-check` and `ddocs validate` on the project docs pass; the PR body has a `Delivers:` line.

Fleet cost rule (prime, via pm-001, 06 Nov 12:22): `just shared-build` runs every cargo command under `nice -n 19` and, where it exists (macOS), `taskpolicy -b`, so no seat can forget the prefix. Wrappers are launched by absolute path and each is skipped if absent.
value.receipt: assets/evidence/phase-1.md: nice 19 and taskpolicy -b on every cargo command; shared-build test

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Code: crates/daemon/src/community/ (holders, directory, writer), crates/daemon/tests/pr122_review/, the s03 and wave B dogfood notes (governance roles/docs-system/outputs/2026-11/). No migration expected.

value.risk: Two lanes edit the same CLI wiring or skill files.
value.mitigation: Rebase onto main before the PR; small diffs at the seam; pm-001 orders merges.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
